data.body:
LANDED — change 1691, merged as 72682442fc (Gerrit rebased on submit; LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1 both green before Submit).

All five ACs met. Full unit suite green (9813 passed) plus make lint and make typecheck.

Root cause, restated for the record: NOT an anchoring failure, an auth/format error, or a size threshold — advisory finding text was never rendered at all. adapter._summarize's PASS branch published only len(verdict['advisory']) as a count, its 'finding' branch itemised blocking findings only, and _translate_findings discarded each finding's location so no anchor ever reached the Gerrit layer. Compounding it, this Gerrit answers /robotcomments with 'robot comments unsupported', so the one robot comment the bot did post was a dead surface.

FOUR reproductions are recorded on this ticket: 1666 and 1685 (the operator's originals), 1636 (which the original report named as a counter-example — live API state shows it was NOT: comments={} and the same count-only message), and 1691, this fix's own review, which published '3 advisory finding(s) (non-blocking)' with comments={} while I watched.

IMPORTANT operational note: advisory visibility on Gerrit begins with the NEXT review AFTER the review bot is redeployed from this merge. Reviews already cast — including 1691's own — are unchanged; their finding text remains only in the durable code_review artifact. The operator's promotion-decision workflow (choosing which advisory criteria to move to the blocking lane) depends on that redeploy, so it is the gating step before the advisory corpus starts accumulating in a readable place.

Scope honesty: the message body is the guaranteed surface and is fully covered by tests. The inline-comment layer is verified against a fake Gerrit, not against a live server — its first real exercise will be that next review, and the fallback path is designed so that if inline posting is rejected the vote still lands with the findings enumerated and an explicit notice.
